proposed.explanation: The investor has a low willingness and ability to accept losses, wants to preserve capital and draw income, and critically needs about 30,000 EGP in liquidity within 6 months. Currently, the investor holds 1,000 shares of COMI at a price of 128.00 EGP per share (totaling 128,000 EGP) and 5,000 EGP in cash, giving a total portfolio value of 133,000 EGP. To meet the liquidity need of 30,000 EGP within 6 months while only having 5,000 EGP in cash, the investor must raise 25,000 EGP from their holdings. Selling 235 shares of COMI at 128.00 EGP raises 30,080 EGP, which combined with the existing 5,000 EGP in cash provides enough liquidity for the 6-month need and leaves a small cash buffer. After selling 235 shares, the investor retains 765 shares of COMI worth 97,920 EGP and holds 35,080 EGP in cash (total portfolio value 133,000 EGP), meaning COMI constitutes approximately 73.6% of the portfolio. While this exceeds the 50% diversification guideline, the immediate mandatory liquidity need of 30,000 EGP within 6 months overrides typical holding preferences. Financial figures for COMI show net profit for the year ending Dec. 31, 2025 of 82,258,815 thousand EGP and basic earnings per share of 18.25 EGP, but these strong fundamentals do not alter the urgent personal liquidity constraint.

claims.statement: Financial figures for COMI show net profit for the year ending Dec. 31, 2025 of 82,258,815 thousand EGP.
Basic earnings per share for the period ended Dec. 31, 2025 was 18.25 EGP.

limitations: Stock prices can fluctuate, meaning the exact amount raised from selling COMI shares may vary if executed at different market prices.
This guidance is based strictly on the provided financial reports and investor profile up to November 2026 and does not guarantee future returns.
